text: Poultry housing (កន្លែងចិញ្ចឹមបសុបក្សី) should protect birds from heat, heavy rain, predators, rodents, and wild birds while allowing good airflow -- a smallholder house doesn't need to resemble a commercial building. During the wet season, the main risks are wet litter, mud, poor drainage, and contaminated water; correct or replace heavily wet litter rather than letting it accumulate, but don't seal the house so tightly that ventilation suffers. During the dry season, heat, dust, and dehydration matter most -- provide shade and airflow. Avoid overcrowding, which increases stress, contamination, and disease spread; there is no single universal stocking density, since it depends on species, age, and housing design. Free-ranging/scavenging birds are common for Cambodian smallholders -- complete separation from wild birds isn't realistic, so focus on reducing unnecessary contact around feed, water, and nighttime housing instead. New birds should be kept separate and observed before mixing (isolation period set by disease risk and veterinary guidance, not a fixed number); sick birds should be separated promptly. Dead birds must be removed immediately and never left where other animals can access them or fed to other animals. Sudden mortality or rapidly spreading respiratory/neurological disease is an urgent warning sign -- minimize movement and seek veterinary help; never assume a specific symptom proves Newcastle disease or avian influenza. Do not assume a dominant local chicken/duck breed for Preah Vihear -- record the farmer's actual bird type.
